analysis:
The PR adds an optional stopStringScope (CBv2StopStringScope?) that is plumbed through the bridge: EngineV2Bridge.swift stores it as a constructor property (lines 109-111, 374, 435), EngineV2Translation.cbv2Request forwards it into CBv2Request (head lines 68-69, 83-84), and EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift accepts it on the submit entry points and sets it on the request (line ~254). The head excerpt for Submission, lines 536-1002, shows runPump receiving stopStringScope: cbv2Request.stopStringScope at line 948, alongside stopSequences.

The change only affects where client stop strings are matched (reasoning scope versus the whole output). It adds no new data egress, logging, key handling, cache-scope, or attestation behavior. cacheSalt and prefixCacheEnabled in the T-041 path are unchanged. The request's stop strings come from the existing request.stop field, and no new untrusted input surface is introduced beyond an enum scope. The shared-KV, prefix-staging, and retirement-transfer unwind paths visible in the Submission excerpt are context only and were not modified by this diff. I saw no regression in T-041 cache isolation, cancellation or retirement handling (T-010), or plaintext response handling (T-008).

Open integration questions: the engine-side implementation of CBv2StopStringScope and the pump's stop handling are outside the supplied units, so the effect of stopping on text within versus outside the reasoning scope is unverified. The only plausible concern is a semantic one: a stop string might fail to truncate output in the hidden-reasoning portion, which is not a security boundary here. The Submission patch excerpt is truncated at the line-254 change, so the final argument passed there was not seen in full.
